dedupe_keys.name: road corridor risk from extreme heat and pluvial flooding in holdfast bay south australia erad project 2026

description: This case assessed how extreme heat and pluvial flooding threaten a council's road corridors under climate change and how treatments would change the risk, to support resilience investment decisions. It was part of the Enhanced Resilient Asset Delivery (ERAD) project led by CSIRO with the City of Holdfast Bay, Resilient South, Value Advisory Partners, Adelaide University, Monash and Swinburne universities, The Systems Cooperative and the South Australian Fire and Emergency Services Commission, following the Enabling Resilience Investment approach. Adelaide University examined four hazard and asset pairs in a focal area of Holdfast Bay: heat and the road surface layer (rutting), flooding and the road sub-base, heat and walking and cycling, and heat and street trees. Methods included the Beecroft pavement temperature model, the MEPDG rutting model with traffic surveys, vulnerability curves for active transport against heat exposure and shade, and WhichPlantWhere climate suitability for tree species, under baseline and climate scenarios. The technical report (February 2026) and literature review are free to read online on Adelaide University's figshare under CC BY 4.0; model inputs are not released. Outcome: walking and cycling on the corridors was projected to fall by 5.1% to 6.85% under RCP 2.6 and 5.8% to 7.7% under RCP 8.5 from heat, and 773 trees of 27 species were rated suitable for 2030; treatments such as heat-resistant binders and climate-suited species were evaluated. Limitations: one focal area and council-specific inputs. The case shows risk assessment and adaptation planning for local roads, and complements the Dalton Highway and US rail hazard records catalogued here.
name: Road corridor risk from extreme heat and pluvial flooding in Holdfast Bay, South Australia (ERAD project, 2026)
